claims.statement: EEA identifies water audits, leak repair, efficient devices, reuse, digital modelling, and smart controls as savings routes. A founder can enter through installer-placed submeters and a signed share-of-savings baseline, but control of a customer's water data and remediation work has not been secured.

The measurable loss is paid water and associated energy consumed above a weather-, occupancy-, or production-normalized baseline, plus downtime during scarcity. EEA says about 30% of EU land experiences seasonal scarcity and estimates meaningful savings potential in tourism and industry; a Polish target site's actual avoidable bill must be metered.

The first payer hypothesis is a hotel, food processor, car wash, or other water-using SME funding the service from utilities and facility budgets through shared savings. EU strategy sets a 2030 efficiency direction, but low Polish water prices may leave no adequate budget at many sites.

contrary_evidence: Water scarcity is uneven across Europe, and a 10% EU-wide efficiency ambition does not create an immediate Polish purchase mandate.
Utilities, plumbers, equipment suppliers, and energy-service firms can bundle audits and leak detection.

economics.acquisition_route: Use energy-installation partners to identify 20 SMEs with accessible meters, run bill-data screens, and finance submetering only at two sites where a conservative audit shows a short payback and the customer signs a 24-month savings-share contract.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A portfolio of standardized water-performance contracts can compound into a financing and underwriting platform for efficiency retrofits; reaching the founder objective requires repeatable vertical playbooks and third-party hardware capital.
economics.founder_time: About 12-18 hours per week for analysis, contracts, and partner coordination; plumbers and equipment firms execute remedial work.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Share of verified savings less sensors, financing cost, installer work, and measurement disputes; software-only monitoring has better margin after the first retrofit.
economics.payback: Fund only measures with modeled hardware payback under 18 months and contract duration long enough to recover acquisition and monitoring cost.
economics.pricing: No- or low-upfront audit followed by 25-40% of weather/production-normalized savings for 24-36 months; monitoring subscription after the savings term.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Savings share recurs monthly, monitoring persists, and multi-site operators can roll out the same intervention across locations.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Vertical-specific baselines, verified intervention savings, and financing-performance history
fingerprint.customer: Polish hotels, food and beverage SMEs, car washes, and other measurable water-intensive facilities
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Energy installers, plumbers, equipment dealers, and multi-site owner referrals
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Metered water-efficiency retrofit financed from a multi-year share of verified savings
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Facility pays from monthly avoided utility cost once an installed intervention produces verified savings
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A facility's water and related energy use rises above a defensible operational baseline or threatens continuity

founder_fit: The family installation channel offers access to SMEs already buying efficiency equipment.
Baseline construction, anomaly detection, and savings verification fit the founder's data-science strengths.
Projects can be screened before capital is committed, limiting downside.
risks: Savings may be too small relative to sensor, plumbing, financing, and sales costs.
Production and occupancy changes can make baseline disputes difficult.
A financed physical portfolio can consume more capital and operational attention than the founder can spare.

structure.commercial_archetype: Financed outcome contract for resource efficiency
structure.control_point: Installed submeter, agreed normalized baseline, and exclusive share-of-savings remediation contract
structure.critical_dependency: Sufficient avoidable spend and a baseline robust enough for both sides to accept monthly savings

thesis: Backcast from water efficiency becoming a financed resilience asset: acquire the measurement-and-savings contract now at small commercial sites, then let verified intervention data unlock cheaper capital and vertical playbooks.
title: Water Savings Covenant
uncertainties: Which Polish SME vertical has the best combination of avoidable water cost, repeatability, and short sales cycles is unknown.
Customer credit quality and willingness to sign multi-year savings shares need testing.
No insurer or funder has confirmed that verified data lowers financing cost.
